Best Family Vacations In Mexico

By Priya Anand · March 28, 2026 · Updated August 12, 2026

For a lot of North American families, Mexico is the first international trip with kids — and the Riviera Maya in particular has built an entire industry around making that trip easy. All-inclusive resorts here do more of the planning for you than almost anywhere else in the world.

This guide covers the areas worth choosing between, what’s actually worth doing beyond the resort pool, and the handful of practical details that catch first-time visitors out.

Why Mexico is an easy first international trip

Mexico solves a lot of the friction that usually comes with international family travel: short flights from most of North America, resort areas built specifically around all-inclusive family stays, and a genuinely huge range of options at every budget.

The Riviera Maya — the coastline running south from Cancún through Playa del Carmen to Tulum — is the region most built for family travel, with the highest concentration of all-inclusive resorts anywhere in the country.

Best areas to stay

Cancún's Hotel Zone

The most convenient option — short airport transfer, calm water on the lagoon side, and the widest range of resorts. Busier and more built-up than areas further south.

Playa del Carmen / Riviera Maya

A 45–60 minute drive from the airport, with a walkable downtown (Fifth Avenue) alongside the resort strip — a good middle ground between convenience and character.

Tulum

More boutique and design-focused, generally better suited to families with older kids or teens than toddlers, given fewer big-resort kids' clubs.

Things kids can do

  • Xcaret and Xel-Há eco-parks — a full day of snorkeling, rivers, and wildlife exhibits, extremely popular with families
  • Swimming in a cenote (freshwater sinkhole) — a genuinely different experience from the ocean, and a highlight for most kids 5+
  • Chichén Itzá day trips, though the heat and walking suit older kids better than toddlers
  • Snorkeling along the Mesoamerican Reef, the second-largest reef system in the world

Travel tips

  • Tap water isn't safe to drink — resorts provide purified water, but be mindful with ice and produce if you venture off-resort
  • Airport transfers are worth pre-booking rather than arranging on arrival, especially with young kids and luggage
  • December through April is dry season and the most reliable weather; June through November carries hurricane risk
  • A basic passport is required for US citizens flying to Mexico, including infants

Frequently asked questions

Is Cancún or the Riviera Maya better for families?

Cancún's Hotel Zone is more convenient for a short airport transfer and has calm lagoon-side water; the Riviera Maya (Playa del Carmen area) offers more walkable town character alongside similar resort quality.

Is Mexico safe for a family vacation?

The resort areas of Cancún and the Riviera Maya see millions of family visitors annually and have a well-established tourism infrastructure. As anywhere, sticking to well-known resort areas and using official transportation is sensible.

What documents do kids need to travel to Mexico?

A valid passport is required for all travelers, including infants, when flying between the US and Mexico. If only one parent is traveling with the child, some airlines and border agents may ask for a notarized consent letter from the other parent.
